Fed’s Waller Hints at Interest Rate Pause as Inflation Cools

In a speech delivered Thursday, Governor Waller signaled that incoming inflation data would dictate the central bank’s next interest rate decision, emphasizing that if recent cooling trends in prices continue, monetary policy may not require additional tightening.

Waller noted that while policymakers remain vigilant, recent economic indicators show encouraging progress on underlying inflation, easing fears among equity investors of immediate rate hikes at the upcoming September FOMC meeting.
Falling Treasury Yields Fuel Bloom Energy and Clean Tech Surge

The dovish interpretation of Waller’s remarks triggered a pullback in benchmark Treasury yields across the curve, with the 10-year Treasury yield easing to around 4.75%. For high-growth companies like Bloom Energy, falling yields reduce capital costs for large-scale energy infrastructure deployments.

Lower discount rates also enhance the present valuation of future cash flows, prompting a sector-wide rally across clean technology and renewable energy stocks that previously faced heavy valuation pressure under higher interest rates.
